title: Speaker-tailored neural speech recognition outperforms familiar listeners for a woman with global aphasia and dysarthria (single case)
summary: A CNN trained only on one patient's voice recognized 72.65% of her words versus 56.75% for 12 familiar professionals; lab result only.
account: A 34-year-old right-handed woman took part in a single-case proof of concept at the University of Messina and IRCCS Centro Neurolesi Bonino-Pulejo. It appears in Frontiers in Rehabilitation Sciences (2026). She has right hemiparesis, global aphasia and dysarthria from a massive left-hemisphere hemorrhage at age 19. A compact convolutional neural network in the CapisciAMe voice-input communication app was trained only on her voice. Training used 1,120 utterances of 13 Italian target words from 33 sessions in one month in a therapy room. Utterances from November 2022 (day not given, so 1 November is used) were the held-out test set. The tailored recognizer identified 680 of 936 test utterances (72.65%). 12 rehabilitation professionals who knew her averaged 56.75%. No real-world communication use is documented.
purpose: Recognize the impaired speech of a person with aphasia and dysarthria so a communication aid can voice her intended words
system: CapisciAMe speaker-dependent ASR (compact convolutional neural network, cnn-trad-fpool3) in a voice-input voice-output communication aid
developer: University of Messina and IRCCS Centro Neurolesi Bonino-Pulejo research team (CapisciAMe app developed in Italy as a research tool)
segment: Adults with post-stroke aphasia and dysarthria
taxonomy_note: The recognizer is a communication aid for a woman with dysarthria, but only a laboratory accuracy result is documented.

ratings.reason: The result is a recognition-accuracy capability measured in test sessions. The paper documents no use of the system for the patient's real communication.
Single-case proof of concept with a 13-word vocabulary.

ai_role.statement: The personalized network is the entire intervention. Its 72.65% word accuracy exceeded the 56.75% mean of familiar listeners. The comparison used a 13-word closed set. The authors state the single-case design and limited vocabulary constrain generalization.
